nytimes_articles.headline: For Both Camps in Final Debate, Hopes, Risks and a Few Surprises
nytimes_articles.abstract: Objectives of Pres Clinton's and Bob Dole's camps in San Diego debate were more subtle and basic than candidates' handlers led public to believe; Dole's aides wanted him to pointedly raise questions about Clinton's character, but advised against overkill that would revive 'hatchet man' image; best hope was that Clinton would be goaded into losing his temper; Clinton aides counseled him to keep cool and not engage in dialogue on ethics, hoping that Dole would be so nasty he would come across as desperate and unseemly, but Clinton would not appear to be ducking the issues; both sides claim victory, Dole raising ethics questions while displaying humor and Clinton maintaining Presidential bearing; graph showing debate ratings were higher than those for baseball playoff game (M)
